subject: Pilot ops: token/batching verification & billing guardrails
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Wong <lara@biometrics.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Pilot ops: token/batching verification & billing guardrails

Hi Lara,

Thanks again for agreeing to the 4-week pilot. Attached is the MAP spreadsheet (pilot-MAP-v2.xlsx) with the eval plan and the specific billing assumptions we use to model expected spend during the trial. Before we lock dates, I want to confirm a couple of operational inputs so our token/$ model matches your real traffic: 

- Representative call profile: you noted 2 request types (short lookup ~120 tokens, long transcript ~3.2k tokens). Can you confirm % split (short vs long) during peak?
- QPS shape: what's your typical peak qps and sustained qps in peak window (per-region)?
- Caching behavior: do you expect a high cache hit rate on repeated lookups? If so, any TTLs we should assume (seconds/minutes)?
- Batching tolerance: internal inference can batch up to X requests, but client latency SLOs matter. Are you comfortable with batching latency up to 120ms tail?

Assumptions we put into the attached MAP (highlighted tab):
- Per-token cost (hosted): $0.000018/token for generation (model: redwood-open-13B q4).
- Baseline KV/prefix cache hit: 35% (saves ~0.7 tokens per lookup on average across patterns).
- Batch size target: 8 concurrent requests (reduces per-token cost by ~18% in our benchmark).
- Cold-start/uncached penalty: 30% extra tokens/time for first 24 hours of a new user cohort.

Ask: please review the highlighted assumptions and either confirm or paste a 72-hour sample of logs (JSONL preferred) so we can re-run the token model on your actual distribution. Attaching the MAP now.

If this looks OK, we'll lock the pilot start for 2027-04-04 and produce a pre-pilot cost snapshot and runbook.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mailto:tessa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: pilot-MAP-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet with assumptions and rollout timeline)
From: Lara Wong <lara@biometrics.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 12:13:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ops: token/batching verification & billing guardrails

Tessa,

Appreciate the clarity here — the MAP looks very close to how we see things. Quick answers inline: 

- Profile split: during peak traffic (US-east) it's roughly 70% short lookup, 30% long transcript. Outside peak it's ~85/15.
- QPS: Peak sustained ~60 qps (we can burst to ~120 qps for short windows); sustained at night ~5 qps.
- Caching: For lookups we expect high TTLs (few minutes) and estimate a 50% hit rate on repeated records within a user session.
- Batching tolerance: 120ms tail is okay for our non-interactive backfill. For interactive flows we need <60ms p95. We can route interactive through a lower-latency config.

I attached a trimmed sample of request logs (sample-usage-logs.jsonl) — note we scrubbed PII. There's one caveat: our long transcripts are sometimes tokenized into many small prompt pieces (so the effective token count is higher than the raw transcript length). Can you account for that in the model?

We'll aim to start the pilot on 2027-04-06 instead of the 4th — gives us two extra days to finish central approvals.

Thanks,
Lara
Director of Product, Biometrics AI
Attachments: sample-usage-logs.jsonl (trimmed, scrubbed)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:02:00 +00:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot ops: token/batching verification & billing guardrails

Tessa / Rishi — quick calc based on Lara's sample:

- Using their split (70/30 peak) and our per-token 0.000018 estimate, projected daily spend at 60 qps peak (10% of day) is ~$220/day before caching.
- Applying the 50% cache hit rate reduces generation tokens by an estimated 28% overall => revised ~$158/day.
- If we can batch to avg size 6 for short lookups during peak windows, that reduces per-token CPU by ~12% in bench => projected ~$139/day.

Notes / questions for pricing team before we share the pilot invoice template:
1) Do we provide a capped pilot budget (e.g., $5k) or charge actual usage with weekly checkpoints?
2) For their interactive flow we should provision a lower-latency pool at slightly higher per-token rate; recommend we put a flag in the MAP to route <60ms flows to dedicated nodes.

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with the recalculated numbers and add a tab with two pricing options (capped vs actual).

- Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Lara Wong <lara@biometrics.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@biometrics.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 23:42:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Pilot ops: token/batching verification & billing guardrails

Thanks, team — received your notes and the updated MAP. Procurement has approved the $5k capped pilot approach; we want to avoid surprises. We'll send the signed MSA addendum tomorrow and share 72 hours of raw request logs (as requested).

Two operational asks for Redwood: 
- Please include a short runbook step in the MAP for how we can temporarily disable batching for an individual user/session (we'll use this to debug latency-sensitive customers).
- Can you surface a per-route token breakdown in the console for pilot users (helps our product team understand where tokens spike)?

Once we have the signed addendum, let's plan a kickoff for 2027-04-06.

Best,
Lara
